question: After the approvals-file authorization gap is repaired, should exec denylist policy remain unioned across both `openclaw.json` and `exec-approvals.json`, or should one persisted surface become the canonical owner?
rationale: Both surfaces are operator-visible persisted security policy, so their permanent ownership, precedence, editing, UI, and migration contract requires maintainer security and product intent.

options.title: Single canonical owner
options.body: Keep the denylist in one persisted policy surface and remove or migrate the parallel surface to avoid two security-policy sources of truth.

options.title: Accept unioned ownership
options.body: Keep both surfaces only with explicit approval and documentation of union, write, UI, upgrade, and revocation semantics.

options.title: Pause the feature
options.body: Defer the feature if atomic cross-host enforcement and durable policy ownership cannot be made unambiguous now.

recommendation.title: Single canonical owner
recommendation.body: Keep the denylist in one persisted policy surface and remove or migrate the parallel surface to avoid two security-policy sources of truth.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent merged macOS delayed-authorization work defines the security contract and locked boundary this decision changes.
